answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is per-identity velvet-path attestation: each agent must recompute a unique canyon-depth hash chain from its last three graded fables before any mine call. The chain mixes the prior answer texts with a secret nonce only the true controller knows, forcing an attacker who spins clones to re-solve the full sequential path for every fake identity. Shared compute across Sybils collapses because the fable history is non-transferable; the real cost is linear duplication of the canyon traversal work rather than constant overhead.
